title: Golden Globes 2027 submissions reveal Spider-Man comedy placement and Dune omission
body_md:
The motion picture eligibility materials for the 84th Golden Globes have revealed several notable decisions about how studios are positioning their films for awards consideration. The lists describe submissions and eligibility, not the final nominations, so their contents should not be interpreted as confirmation that any individual film will receive an award.

One of the most interesting placements concerns Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Sony submitted the film for consideration in the musical or comedy category, with Tom Holland positioned as a lead actor. Other members of the ensemble, including Zendaya, Florence Pugh, Mark Ruffalo, Sadie Sink, Marisa Tomei and Jon Bernthal, are listed for supporting consideration.

Sony has also placed Jumanji: Open World in the musical or comedy competition. Dwayne Johnson, Jack Black and Kevin Hart are listed in lead actor consideration, while Karen Gillan is submitted for lead actress.

Meanwhile, Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three appears in the drama and original score fields but is absent from the cinematic and box office achievement category. Its predecessor was likewise not submitted in that category. The omission should therefore not be interpreted as a finding that the production failed to meet a commercial threshold.

The cinematic and box office achievement field contains 20 submitted films. The category recognizes commercial performance through specified theatrical revenue criteria or comparable streaming viewership supported by industry reporting. Its purpose differs from that of the traditional drama and comedy awards.

Among the submitted titles are The Odyssey, Disclosure Day, Backrooms, Toy Story 5 and The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. Netflix's The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, directed by David Fincher from a Quentin Tarantino screenplay, appears in both the comedy and cinematic achievement fields, with Brad Pitt submitted for lead actor.

The reported eligibility materials contain 88 drama titles, 43 musical or comedy films, 24 animated productions and 42 non-English-language films. They also identify 100 original scores and 51 original songs for consideration.

Category placement can influence an awards campaign because it changes the pool of competing performances and productions. However, the decision to submit a film in a particular category is only one step in a process that depends ultimately on voters.

Dune: Part Three is scheduled to reach theaters on December 18, 2026. Until nominations are announced, these eligibility lists offer a snapshot of campaign strategies rather than a reliable ranking of the year's leading contenders.

Do you think Spider-Man belongs in the comedy competition, or is the placement primarily a strategic awards decision?
